As part of ongoing consultations between the Islamic Consultative Assembly (Parliament) and the Iranian Ministry of Foreign Affairs on the country’s foreign policy and national security issues, a meeting was held on Monday afternoon between Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi and the Tehran Province parliamentary delegation. During the meeting, the foreign minister outlined the latest regional and international developments and provided a report on the key measures and initiatives undertaken by the diplomatic apparatus to safeguard the country’s national interests. Araghchi stressed that, while pursuing Iran’s national rights and interests at the international level, the diplomatic apparatus is seriously pursuing the use of diplomatic capabilities to safeguard national interests. The foreign minister also outlined the country’s foreign policy priorities, emphasizing the importance of developing relations with neighboring and regional countries, expanding economic cooperation with various countries, leveraging economic diplomacy to neutralize sanctions, and strengthening public and media diplomacy to explain the positions and views of the Islamic Republic of Iran. During the meeting, Tehran Province MPs presented their views and concerns on various foreign policy issues and raised questions regarding certain foreign policy matters, which the foreign minister answered. Members of the Tehran Province parliamentary delegation highlighted the need to preserve national unity and cohesion and support the diplomatic apparatus’s efforts to safeguard national interests. They also stressed the importance of synergy among the branches of government and mobilizing all national capacities to counter threats and advance the objectives of the Islamic Republic of Iran.

item.title: Iranian Foreign Ministry statement condemning Britains baseless accusations Against Iran
item.description: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran strongly condemns the claims made by British officials attributing the alleged security incident at RAF Fairford to Iran, describing them as an ugly plot to advance an anti-Iran campaign and evade accountability for Britain's participation in the US-Zionist military aggression against the Iranian people. The British government cannot evade its political and legal responsibility for its claims and their potential consequences by hiding behind ambiguous language without providing solid evidence and substantiated reasons. Resorting to expressions such as “highly likely” and “almost certainly” to create the impression that attributing the alleged incident to Iran is credible, is an obvious attempt to escape accountability for making baseless accusations. Britain's track record of fabricating security claims against other countries, which have in some cases led to damaging tensions and conflicts in West Asia, is well known. The British government must be held accountable for persisting in this approach, which undermines international peace and security. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran categorically rejects the baseless accusations leveled against Iran and holds the British government, as well as the designers and perpetrators of this clumsy false-flag operation, responsible for all consequences arising from these fabrications.

item.title: Iranian Saudi FMs discuss regional developments by phone
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi and Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan held a telephone conversation on Sunday night to discuss and exchange views on ongoing developments in the region. Expressing concern over escalating tensions, the Iranian foreign minister stressed that insisting on a military approach and disregarding a political solution would further complicate the existing situation. Araghchi also emphasized that the ongoing crises in the region have no military solution, stressing that the Islamic Republic of Iran is ready to provide any assistance to help initiate dialogue between Saudi Arabia and Yemen and facilitate the achievement of a political solution.

item.title: Baghaei warns Europe against complicity in US attack on law justice
item.description:
Rubio threatens to dismantle the ICC “brick by brick” if U.S. allies fail to rein it in. Remember the 1930s: international orders collapse not only through aggression, but when the use of force becomes normalized and the world remains silent. Europe! Does standing by an alliance mean defending international law and the post-WWII normative & institutional framework - or standing with the U.S. as it dismantles them? If law & justice are sacrificed to appease an aggressive ally, any talk of human rights and a rules-based international order becomes nothing more than empty rhetoric.

item.description:

Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesman Esmail Baghaei said on X that U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio was distorting history to provide a philosophical and historical justification for U.S. warmongering. At the Acropolis, Marco Rubio (mis)presents the history of the West - from ancient Greece to the contemporary United States - as a single, seamless continuum. This is the logic of anachronism: a distortion of historical time produced by the careless fusion of categories such as Greece, Rome, Christianity, Europe, America, and, ultimately, “America First.” It is as if America has finally discovered that 'intimidation' can be staged more effectively beneath the neon lights of a philosophy of history than in the bare idiom of the cowboy. Rubio lifts the Greek concept of 'thumos' out of its historical and philosophical setting and recasts it as a celebration of power - of force exercised without law or justice - along with competition and national will. That reading misses a constitutive half of the Greek inheritance. Greece was not only a theater of power and glory. It was also the birthplace of the tragedy of hubris and aggression, from the myth of Troy and Homer’s Iliad; of the critique of imperial ambition in Thucydides’ History of the Peloponnesian War; of political philosophy in Plato’s Republic and Aristotle’s Politics; and of enduring meditations on the limits of power, moral responsibility, and human fate in Sophocles’ Antigone and Oedipus Rex. This other half of the Greek legacy is deliberately omitted from Rubio’s narrative. History is thereby converted from a field of inquiry and critical reflection into an instrument of political legitimation. What emerges is not a philosophy of history, but a manufactured narrative designed to authorize U.S. militancy and to construct a convenient political myth: a distorted reconstruction of the past in which the politics of the present are made to appear inevitable and historically ordained. Once history is pressed into the service of legitimizing power—the unlawful and unjust use of force—its purpose is no longer to understand the past, but to glorify power itself. Vasily Vereshchagin’s The Apotheosis of War offers a stark counter-image. Its pyramid of skulls, left behind by conquerors, confronts the mythology of glory with the material residue of conquest. It recalls what remains when history is reduced to the exaltation of power. At such a juncture, Western thinkers have a responsibility to defend history itself - and the philosophical complexity of Western civilization - against a distorted and apologetic reinterpretation by an aggressive power prepared to sacrifice a civilization’s human achievements in order to legitimize the unrestrained exercise of force. The danger lies not merely in misreading the past, but in appropriating it to authorize that force, and to aggrandize it, in the present.

As part of the ongoing consultations between the Islamic Consultative Assembly and the diplomatic apparatus on various foreign policy issues, a meeting was held on Tuesday evening with the participation of Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi and a number of members of the Islamic Consultative Assembly. During the three-hour meeting, attended by Ali Babaei Karnamei, Chairman of the Social Affairs Commission, and a number of respected members of the Islamic Consultative Assembly, the Foreign Minister presented a comprehensive report on the discussions and activities undertaken during the delegation of the Islamic Republic of Iran’s visit to New York to attend the 81st annual session of the United Nations General Assembly. Referring to his and the President’s numerous consultations with various countries participating in the UN General Assembly, the Foreign Minister stressed that the delegation of the Islamic Republic of Iran, backed by the heroic resistance and steadfastness of the Iranian people in the face of the military aggression of its enemies, articulated Iran’s positions in the clearest and most authoritative manner possible. The Foreign Minister also referred to the use of the opportunity provided by the UN General Assembly session to explain Iran’s innovative approach and present a seven-day plan for restoring security to the Strait of Hormuz. He stressed that, based on instructions issued by the competent authorities of the country, the delegation of the Islamic Republic of Iran presented Iran’s conditions and considerations to the mediators in the form of a precise and operational plan. It became clear to all that, just as the Islamic Republic of Iran is resolute and determined in defending itself, it is also serious about using the tools of diplomacy to safeguard its national interests and security. During the meeting, the Foreign Minister also responded to questions and discussed the proposals and views of the members of Parliament, providing explanations on a wide range of foreign policy and national security issues, including economic diplomacy, neutralizing sanctions, relations with neighboring countries, strengthening public and media diplomacy, documenting war crimes committed by the United States and the Israeli regime, and pursuing the demand for justice and retribution for the martyrs of the Second and Third Imposed Wars. The members of Parliament expressed their appreciation for the efforts and initiatives of the diplomatic apparatus in safeguarding national interests and the rights of the Iranian people, and stressed the need for continued collective efforts to preserve national unity and cohesion, as well as simultaneous support for both the field and diplomacy in defense of Iran’s sovereignty and integrity.

item.title: Baghaei: False-flag operations cannot conceal illegal US-Israeli wars
item.description: Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Esmail Baghaei wrote on X that false-flag operations cannot conceal the illegal and criminal nature of the endless wars waged by the United States and the Israeli regime, saying the perpetrators are resorting to lies as they struggle to justify their aggression against Iran. The message is as follows: False flags are an old craft: manufacture the incident, assign the blame, and harvest the consequences. In a world where the American and international public is weary of an unlawful war of aggression against Iran, and where the aggressors have no honest way to justify a war of choice, even a raft made of lies can look like salvation to those who are drowning.

item.title: Iranian MFA Spokesperson writes on X after meeting new German ambassador
item.description: Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Esmail Baghaei wrote on X that he had held candid and useful talks with Germany’s new ambassador to Iran, Axel Dittmann, on developments in international relations and shared responsibility for protecting the rule of law and international peace and security. His message reads as follows: Today, I received the new German Ambassador to Iran, Amb Alex Dittmann, and we had an engaging and frank discussion on prevailing trends in international relations. Countering the threats and challenges that jeopardize the rule of law and endanger international peace and security remains a shared responsibility - one that calls for insight, courage, and cooperation.

item.title: UN Special Envoy for Lebanon meets with Foreign Minister Araghchi

He expressed hope that, with the continued effective role of Iran and other regional parties, an end to the war and the establishment of lasting peace and security in the region, particularly in Lebanon, would be witnessed. Jean Arnault, the UN Special Envoy for Lebanon, who has traveled to Tehran for consultations with Iranian officials, met with Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi on Tuesday morning. During the meeting, Arnault presented his assessment of the latest developments and the situation in Lebanon amid the continuation of the Israeli occupation, as well as efforts undertaken to consolidate the ceasefire and bring the war to an end. He expressed hope that, with the continued effective role of Iran and other regional parties, an end to the war and the establishment of lasting peace and security in the region, particularly in Lebanon, would be witnessed. The Foreign Minister, for his part, emphasized the Islamic Republic of Iran’s principled position in support of Lebanon’s territorial integrity and national sovereignty, and called for the strengthening of the United Nations’ efforts and initiatives to halt the aggression and occupation by the Zionist regime in Lebanon. Araghchi also announced Iran’s readiness to continue consultations and cooperation with the United Nations and regional countries to help maintain stability and security in Lebanon. During his visit, the UN Secretary-General’s representative also held separate meetings with Majid Takht-Ravanchi, Deputy Foreign Minister for Political Affairs, and Mehdi Shoushtari, Assistant Foreign Minister and Director General for West Asia and North Africa at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, during which they held consultations and exchanged views on developments in Lebanon and the region.
